title: Jude and the Wardrobe
premise: After his mother's funeral, Casper Almeida returns to the family house to catalog her belongings and finds a wardrobe that doesn't open onto clothes but onto the remembered rooms of a life she never narrated. Inside, he encounters Odalys, the last fluent speaker of Kiremba, a language his mother helped suppress as a young translator for the courts, and she asks Casper to become her final student before her memory fails entirely. As lessons deepen, Casper discovers his mother's silence was not absence but an arranged architecture — a family built around one unasked question about what she did to Odalys's community. In the end, Casper asks it aloud in Kiremba at Odalys's deathbed, receives no forgiveness and something better — witness — and chooses to carry the language forward rather than inherit the quiet.
about_author: Wren Oyelaran is a former court interpreter turned novelist who writes about the debts families settle in languages they refuse to speak. They live between two coastal cities and teach a free weekly class in a dying language that is not their own.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Silence
chapters.summary: Casper, POV, catalogs his mother's possessions three days after the funeral, noting how each object refuses to explain her. The emotional beat is numb competence cracking into grief when he finds a wardrobe key labeled only with a word he can't read.

chapters.title: What the Wardrobe Kept
chapters.summary: Casper opens the wardrobe and steps into a preserved version of his mother's childhood room, where objects play back fragments of memory. POV Casper; beat: wonder shadowed by the sense of trespassing inside someone's refusal.

chapters.title: A Woman Who Counts Words
chapters.summary: In the wardrobe's deepest room, Casper meets Odalys, who has been waiting there in some liminal way since before the funeral. She names the unreadable word: it is Kiremba for 'the question.' Beat: recognition and dread.

chapters.title: First Lesson
chapters.summary: Odalys begins teaching Casper Kiremba through household objects, insisting language is inherited debt. Intercut with Casper's brother Theo demanding he sell the house. Beat: the first pull between duty to family and duty to the dead.

chapters.title: The Translator's Daughter
chapters.summary: Casper learns his mother worked as a court translator in the years before he was born, the same courts that ruled against Odalys's land claims. POV Casper, with wardrobe-flashback interludes. Beat: the almost-said thing takes shape.

chapters.title: Theo's Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo arrives to force the estate sale and finds Casper speaking a stranger's language in their mother's bedroom. POV shifts briefly to Theo, revealing his own grief expressed as control. Beat: fraternal rupture.

chapters.title: Words for Water
chapters.summary: Odalys teaches the vocabulary of rivers and boundaries; Casper realizes Kiremba has no word for 'owner,' only words for 'keeper.' Beat: vertigo — his whole inheritance reframed.

chapters.title: The Arrangement
chapters.summary: Casper uncovers letters showing the family knew about the suppressed testimony and organized its silence around it — holidays scheduled, topics banned, his father complicit. Beat: betrayal widening across generations.

chapters.title: Odalys Forgets a Door
chapters.summary: Odalys's memory falters; a room in the wardrobe goes dark and unreachable. Casper understands time is finite and begins recording lessons obsessively. Beat: urgency replacing curiosity.

chapters.title: The Question, Drafted
chapters.summary: Casper writes and burns four drafts of the question in English, unable to say it even on paper. POV Casper; beat: the art of almost saying it reaches its cruelest refinement.

chapters.title: Aunt Vera's Version
chapters.summary: Vera, the family's keeper of acceptable history, visits and offers a sanitized account of Casper's mother's court years. Casper lets her talk, then says one Kiremba word aloud. Beat: quiet insubordination.

chapters.title: Keeper, Not Owner
chapters.summary: Casper researches the land case himself in municipal archives, finding his mother's name on a mistranslated deposition that cost Odalys's community everything. Beat: shame made specific and dated.

chapters.title: The Dark Room
chapters.summary: Another wardrobe chamber closes; Odalys can no longer recall her mother's songs. She teaches Casper the mourning grammar instead. Beat: tenderness under loss, teacher becoming legacy.

chapters.title: Theo Returns
chapters.summary: Theo threatens legal action over the house; Casper realizes the law can transfer property but cannot touch what actually needs settling. Beat: the theme of justice outside the law crystallizes.

chapters.title: Lesson in the Rain
chapters.summary: Odalys leads Casper outside the wardrobe for the first time, to the river from the land case, teaching him to speak to water. Beat: the language becomes lived rather than studied.

chapters.title: What Mother Almost Said
chapters.summary: The wardrobe reveals its final memory: his mother, young, drafting a retraction she never filed, then hiding the key. Beat: compassion for the cowardice without excusing it.

chapters.title: The Family Gathers
chapters.summary: Casper convenes the relatives and, instead of the will reading they expect, plays recordings of the lessons. The arrangement cracks; some walk out, Vera stays. Beat: the silence publicly broken.

chapters.title: The Question
chapters.summary: At Odalys's deathbed, Casper asks the question in full Kiremba: what do you require of me for what my mother did? She answers that being asked, finally, in her own tongue, is the settlement. Beat: climax — witness instead of absolution.

chapters.title: Last Speaker, First Student
chapters.summary: Odalys dies; the wardrobe empties into ordinary coats and hangers. Casper grieves a teacher the world never counted. Beat: desolation transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: The House Stays
chapters.summary: Casper declines to sell, offering Theo instead the truth in writing and a share of nothing material. Theo, shaken by the recordings, does not fight. Beat: reconciliation without erasure.

chapters.title: Tuesday Class
chapters.summary: Months later, Casper teaches Kiremba to five strangers in the house's front room, using his mother's furniture as vocabulary. Beat: inheritance redirected — belonging built rather than received.

chapters.title: The Word on the Key
chapters.summary: Casper engraves the Kiremba word for 'question' onto a new key and leaves the wardrobe unlocked. Final image: a student arriving, asking what the word means. Beat: the almost-said becomes the invitation.
